paragraphs: He was a student of Rava, as in Niddah 46a, [where it is said] that he would recite Rava's teaching in this formulation.

And in Bava Metzia 49a: Rav Papi said: Ravina told me: One of the Sages told me personally — Rav Tavut was his name, and some say Rav Shmuel bar Zutra was his name — [a man such] that if they were to give [him] (Hyman prints: "me") the entire expanse of the world, he would not deviate in his speech: "Such a case happened to me. On a certain day — it was the afternoon of a Sabbath eve — I was sitting, and a certain man came and stood at the door. He said to me: Do you have sesame seeds to sell? I said to him: No. He said to me: Let these zuz be with you as a deposit. I said to him: Here is the house before you. He placed them in the house, and they were stolen. He came before Rava, etc."
And he is mentioned in Shabbat 23a in the wording: "as R' Shmuel bar Zutra taught: All oils are fine, etc."; "R' Shmuel bar Zutra recited it thus, etc."

notes.text: The nested anecdote prints “me” where its surrounding characterization speaks about the named sage in the third person. That change of person is retained.

All explicit full Rav titles are retained in the heading and Bava Metzia report; Rava and Ravina remain names. In both Shabbat occurrences the supplied ר״ש is contextually Shmuel with abbreviated title R', rather than an independently verified full Rav or a new identity. The older Shimon expansion and the earlier full-Rav rendering remain in historical versions. Hyman's student-of-Rava statement and the reciting interpretation of שמתני remain attributed to his notice; Niddah 46a and Shabbat 23a have not been newly checked. The whole saved 439-character Davidson Bava Metzia 49a scalar explicitly has Rav Papi, Rav Tavut and the alternative Rav Shmuel bar Zutra, and supports told me personally and third-person ליה, him. Hyman's supplied לי, me, remains visible beside the bracketed readability rendering [him]; supplied replaces printed in the new English because no printed pixels or correction history were inspected. The supplied כדידי beside the digital בדידי and supplied חוה beside the digital הוה are retained as source differences without Hebrew repair or a printing-history claim. The nested scholar's first-person story and the introductory third-person characterization remain distinct; the two alternative names are not merged. The selected scalar ends at the sesame-sale question: the later negative answer, plural zuz deposit, put them in the house, theft, coming before Rava and final etc. are translated from Hyman's supplied continuation, not claimed as freshly verified in that scalar. No window, extra legal outcome or unprovided continuation is added. All old English, current and carried notes, original responses and the p003 source hold are retained.

The consulted scan of Hyman III, printed p. 1136, confirms li, “me,” in the introductory characterization, whereas the whole Davidson Bava Metzia 49a passage reads leih, “him”; the bracketed English keeps this difference visible. The print also has bedidi and havah beside the supplied transcription’s כדידי and חוה. The story continues into 49b: the refusal to sell sesame, deposit of the zuz, placing them in the house, theft and appearance before Rava have now been read in full. “He placed them” is the narrative action in the consulted translation; the English no longer adds an instruction to put them there. Hyman’s abbreviated ending is retained without adding the ensuing legal discussion. The whole Niddah 46a passage confirms that Shmuel bar Zutra recites Rava’s teaching, and the whole Shabbat 23a passage names him in both recitation formulas, distinguishing oils from smoke. His studentship remains Hyman’s inference, the two alternative names remain alternatives, and the abbreviated source titles remain as represented. The earlier notes describe the preceding, more limited inspection and remain unchanged.
